title: 17. Numeracy & Number Systems: Division with Remainders
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the quotient and remainder when a two-digit number is divided by a one-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(17\div 5\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(17\) by \(5\). Since \(5\times 3=15\), the quotient is \(3\). Subtract \(17-15=2\), so the remainder is \(2\). Therefore, \(17\div 5=3\text{ remainder }2\).
questions.hint: Find the largest multiple of \(5\) that is less than or equal to \(17\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the quotient and remainder when a two-digit number is divided by a one-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(29\div 4\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(29\) by \(4\). Since \(4\times 7=28\), the quotient is \(7\). Subtract \(29-28=1\), so the remainder is \(1\). Therefore, \(29\div 4=7\text{ remainder }1\).
questions.hint: Find the largest multiple of \(4\) that is less than or equal to \(29\).

questions.learningObjective: Find a whole number given its quotient and remainder.
questions.question: A number divided by \(6\) gives quotient \(8\) and remainder \(3\). What is the number?
questions.explanation: Use the relationship \(\text{dividend}=\text{divisor}\times\text{quotient}+\text{remainder}\). Substitute the given values: \(6\times 8+3=48+3=51\). Therefore, the number is \(51\).
questions.hint: Multiply the divisor by the quotient, then add the remainder.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the quotient and remainder when a two-digit number is divided by a one-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(38\div 7\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(38\) by \(7\). Since \(7\times 5=35\), the quotient is \(5\). Subtract \(38-35=3\), so the remainder is \(3\). Therefore, \(38\div 7=5\text{ remainder }3\).
questions.hint: Find the largest multiple of \(7\) that is less than or equal to \(38\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify a division expression that has a given remainder.
questions.question: Which division has a remainder of \(2\)?
questions.explanation: For \(20\div 6\), since \(6\times 3=18\), the remainder is \(20-18=2\). For \(20\div 4\), since \(4\times 5=20\), the remainder is \(0\). Therefore, \(20\div 6\) has a remainder of \(2\).
questions.hint: Find the largest multiple of the divisor that is less than or equal to the dividend.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the quotient and remainder when a two-digit number is divided by a one-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(43\div 8\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(43\) by \(8\). Since \(8\times 5=40\), the quotient is \(5\). Subtract \(43-40=3\), so the remainder is \(3\). Therefore, \(43\div 8=5\text{ remainder }3\).
questions.hint: Find the largest multiple of \(8\) that is less than or equal to \(43\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the quotient and remainder when a two-digit number is divided by a one-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(50\div 9\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(50\) by \(9\). Since \(9\times 5=45\), the quotient is \(5\). Subtract \(50-45=5\), so the remainder is \(5\). Therefore, \(50\div 9=5\text{ remainder }5\).
questions.hint: Find the largest multiple of \(9\) that is less than or equal to \(50\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve a word problem involving division with remainders.
questions.question: There are \(26\) apples. They are packed into bags with \(4\) apples in each full bag. How many full bags can be made, and how many apples are left over?
questions.explanation: Divide \(26\) by \(4\). Since \(4\times 6=24\), there are \(6\) full bags. Subtract \(26-24=2\), so \(2\) apples are left over. Therefore, \(6\) full bags can be made, with \(2\) apples left over.
questions.hint: Divide the total number of apples by the number in each full bag.

questions.learningObjective: Find a whole number given its quotient and remainder.
questions.question: A number divided by \(7\) gives quotient \(9\) and remainder \(5\). What is the number?
questions.explanation: Use the relationship \(\text{dividend}=\text{divisor}\times\text{quotient}+\text{remainder}\). Substitute the given values: \(7\times 9+5=63+5=68\). Therefore, the number is \(68\).
questions.hint: Multiply the divisor by the quotient, then add the remainder.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a word problem involving equal sharing with a remainder.
questions.question: A student has \(59\) stickers. She shares them equally among \(8\) friends. How many stickers does each friend get, and how many stickers are left over?
questions.explanation: Divide \(59\) by \(8\). Since \(8\times 7=56\), each friend gets \(7\) stickers. Subtract \(59-56=3\), so \(3\) stickers are left over. Therefore, each friend gets \(7\) stickers, with \(3\) stickers left over.
questions.hint: Divide the total number of stickers by the number of friends.
